reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Gate 1 skipped (missing-validation finding: the issue is that rate limiting is NOT called). Gate 2: entry point is the public PostgREST API via the anon role; NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is intentionally public — no trust_assumptions entry covers this as trusted. Gate 3: supabase/migrations/ is explicitly in scope and rate-limit enforcement on this RPC is a named key_security_concern. An attacker can trigger this via the public PostgREST endpoint by sending POST /rest/v1/rpc/record_attendance_by_card with a card_id obtained from any NFC reader and the browser-bundle anon key in a tight loop, inserting unlimited alternating in/out records and corrupting attendance history for targeted users. Severity held at Medium: data-integrity impact with no privilege escalation or secret disclosure.
